# Owned-state continuation review data

These are hand-authored synthetic review examples for [N0-05's canonical state/FSM proposal](../../../docs/engine/compatibility-and-core.md#n0-05-bounded-continuation-proposal), drafted on 2026-10-16 for issue 11. The contract remains in the engine page; this directory owns example provenance and integrity only. These files are DATA for review, not an executable parser, public schema, conformance corpus, implementation result or passing V/NG gate.

- `continuations.json` gives literal output-byte prefixes, eligible completed-event cuts, partial hidden parser expectations and exact continuation events. Hex strings contain bytes, not displayed terminal text. Expectations name only the relevant subset of state; a future full-state oracle must also inspect the rest of the inventory.
- `state-transitions.json` gives visually equal prefixes with distinguishing continuations, plus save/reset/buffer/resize/history challenges. Key/resize descriptions are illustrative typed events, not adopted wire spellings.
- `bounds-and-recovery.json` gives exact-bound/one-beyond recipes and forbidden recovery claims. Recipes are finite fixture requirements, not engine output or performance measurements.

All bytes, text, IDs and apparent control syntax are invented here. There are no captured prompts, credentials, home paths, environment values, user transcripts, upstream code or upstream conformance data. Byte helpers used while authoring only encode the literal synthetic strings; no terminal engine or OS process was exercised. No dependencies, Unicode tables, locks, project license or historical evidence are changed.

Source rationale is the finite `px-dev-text-0` output/query/input policy and the complete-state/runtime owners linked above. Proposed expectations are explicit private policy, not quotations or independently verified terminal behavior. Requirement/validation mappings are R07–R13/R15/R16 and V07–V13/V15/V16 as recorded per file. Later v1 grapheme/wide-cell/Unicode18/stacks/reflow are excluded from this dev data; their full oracles remain separately gated.

N0-07 must challenge these expectations independently before turning them into executable assertions. It must enumerate every byte cut/transport partition for short streams while keeping keeper event identities fixed, compare full hidden state plus future effects under exact-tuple continuation, and add seeded bounded long cases. When event segmentation itself changes, compare semantic text/mode/occupancy behavior after aligned prefixes; event-derived IDs, event counters and transaction revisions need not be identical. A scheduling yield is neither a new event nor permission to expose a partial frame under an old frontier. Replay comparisons inspect proposed effects but dispatch none. Two live frontends must never generate extra replies.

[manifest.json](manifest.json) records local SHA-256 integrity and provenance. It does not modify the original shared manifest or old X4/EA1 fixtures. Expectations require contract/oracle review before any change; never regenerate them to make an implementation pass. JSON/static checks establish data integrity only, not NG0, N1, compatibility, performance or recovery certification.
